title: Shakeela Begum v. State of U.P.
coram: Naheed Ara Moonis, J.; Vivek Varma, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; relegated to Section 127 appeal.
headnote: Writ to quash a PVVNL demand notice, restrain coercive recovery, and direct installation of a smart meter is dismissed. After the licensee supplied a final assessment dated 12 February 2020, the Court held that an appeal under Section 127 was available; the petitioner did not dispute that remedy.
facts: Shakeela Begum challenged a 20 September 2019 demand of the Executive Engineer, PVVNL, Meerut, seeking to quash the notice, restrain coercive recovery, and direct installation of a smart meter as per a 5 August 2019 letter. She alleged recovery without supply of the provisional assessment. The licensee said the premises were inspected on 18 July 2019, a provisional assessment issued, objections filed on 28 January 2020, and a final assessment of 12 February 2020 supplied in court.

holding_units.holding: Once a final assessment has been passed and supplied, and the consumer does not dispute the availability of an appeal under Section 127, a writ seeking to quash the demand and restrain recovery is dismissed on the ground of alternative remedy.
holding_units.flag: Counsel and the Court described the remedy as an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Supply Code; Section 127 is of the Electricity Act, 2003.

principle_tags.application: Writ against the demand and coercive recovery dismissed because an appeal under Section 127 was available and was not disputed.
After the final assessment dated 12 February 2020 was supplied in court, the petitioner was relegated to the Section 127 appeal.

not_decided.point: merits of the demand and final assessment
not_decided.note: Dismissed solely on alternative remedy; assessment and recovery not examined.

not_decided.point: mandamus to install a smart meter
not_decided.note: Prayer for installation pursuant to the 5 August 2019 letter not decided.
